headline: Shell, Chevron Shut Gulf Output as Isaias Nears Hurricane Strength
seoTitle: Shell, Chevron Cut Gulf Output Ahead of Isaias
seoDescription: Shell and Chevron shut production at Gulf facilities as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthened and threatened the northern U.S. Gulf Coast.
deck: The companies confirmed offshore shutdowns while the U.S. hurricane center warned of rapid strengthening, storm surge and heavy rain.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Shell shut production and evacuated personnel from five Gulf of Mexico assets as Tropical Storm Isaias approached the northern U.S. Gulf Coast. Chevron also began shutting production at four facilities and moved some personnel ashore, the companies told Reuters.
The U.S. offshore regulator said 511,619 barrels a day, or about 25% of current Gulf oil production, had been shut in by midday October 7.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The company shutdowns and regulator's production figure are confirmed actions. The National Hurricane Center reported 65 mph maximum sustained winds at 4 p.m. Central time on October 7 and forecast Isaias to become a hurricane Thursday morning before landfall late Friday or early Saturday.

The projected intensity, track, storm surge, rainfall and tornado risk remain forecasts and can change. The hurricane center placed parts of the northern Gulf Coast under hurricane, tropical-storm and storm-surge watches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The Gulf supplies a significant share of U.S. oil. Prolonged offshore shutdowns or storm damage can tighten supply and influence global crude and fuel prices, which matter to the import-dependent Philippines through pump prices, transport costs and inflation.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the next hurricane-center advisories, additional evacuation or shutdown figures, actual landfall intensity and timing, and whether offshore production can restart quickly after inspections.
